messages.subject: sempath & fixed factor loading
parts:
Hi all,

I am new to SEM. Thank you very much for developing Lavaan this great package. 

1. I am now using sempath to produce the diagram. I use this syntax (semPaths(Nfit, what="std",residuals=TRUE, intercepts=FALSE,thresholds=FALSE, edge.label.cex = .8)). Regarding the residual, the diagram shown had a two-headed arrow pointing to each indicator. Is that error or disturbance term associated with that indicator? I have seen paper drawing a separate oval for that. Are they the same thing? If so, which is preferred?

2. I am using Lavaan and the factor loading of the first indicator of a latent variable is fixed to 1. But I also see other paper showing the SE, Z-value and p-value for that first indicator. I might be conceptually unclear. Where can I find this information or it can be ignored?

Thank those who spend time reading. Look forward to any advice from you all.

Cheers,
Alan

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: sempath & fixed factor loading
parts: Regarding the residual, the diagram shown had a two-headed arrow pointing to each indicator. Is that error or disturbance term associated with that indicator? I have seen paper drawing a separate oval for that. Are they the same thing? If so, which is preferred?

Yes, that is shorthand for saving space, but it represents the same thing as actually drawing the residual/disturbance term as an explicit latent variable with a factor loading fixed to 1.  Either way, the tracing rules for the double-headed arrow lead to the same model-implied covariance matrix.

2. I am using Lavaan and the factor loading of the first indicator of a latent variable is fixed to 1. But I also see other paper showing the SE, Z-value and p-value for that first indicator. I might be conceptually unclear. Where can I find this information or it can be ignored?

It sounds like in the paper you refer to, they might identify the factor variance by fixing it to 1 instead of freely estimating the factor variance and fixing an arbitrary factor loading to 1.  Both are acceptable and lead to the same model-implied covariance matrix and model fit, but the SEs (and by implication, z tests) are sensitive to which factor loading you fix to 1 (see reference).  So unless you have a substantive reason for choosing a particular indicator to use as the reference for setting the scale of the latent variable, then I would typically recommend fixing the factor variance to 1.  But that is not a software-specific question, so you might want to seek advice on SEMNET (a larger and more general SEM forum).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
